title: Daniel Mays & David Thewlis in The Dumb Waiter - Old Vic - review
transcript: hello i'm paul seven lewis and welcome to one minute theater reviews i'll shortly be reviewing the dumb waiter uh which was produced at the old wicked london and streamed live via zoom an experience which took away much of what should have been a definitive performance of the great harold pinter play but first a reminder that you can be the first to know when i post a new review by subscribing to one minute theater reviews when i heard that daniel mays and david fulis were to play the two bickering hitmen in harold pinter's menacing short play the dumb waiter i didn't hesitate to book it it didn't hurt that jeremy herren was directing sadly for me i decided to watch a live stream performance via zoom so i straight away lost that claustrophobic sense of these two men cooped up in a small basement room which i'm sure was conveyed much better in the old vic theater worse though was the quality of the transmission that's always a danger with a live feed through a medium light swim but i found the action constantly jerked or even froze at one point so i can't offer a fair verdict on the production from what i saw daniel mayes as the questioning gus and david thulis as the rules obsessed ben were perfect for the roles maze like a nervous rabbit fuelless a snarling fox it confirmed to me what a great play this is the way the two hitmen try to obey orders even orders for food coming down the dumb waiter from what is or certainly appears to be a non-existent restaurant above and there's the constant sense that something bad is going to happen as they contemplate their past and forthcoming work killing persons unknown to them and commissioned by mysterious mr wilson who could represent and honor the authoritarian government or well even god and the humor in the arguments these two contrasting characters have there's a lovely row over their use of language is it light the kettle or put the kettle on and then there are the lurid extracts from the tabloid newspaper that ben reads out suggesting a frightening world out there and the grim set looked good too as far as i could tell suggesting a prison cell as much as a basement at a closed down restaurant but as i say too poor a transmission to make a proper judgment so for once i won't give this production a star rating just a warning to avoid zoom when you choose to watch a live stream thank you for watching this slightly unusual review and you can be sure of catching my next review by subscribing to this channel and you can read my reviews at reviews dot co dot uk and now that theaters are over again for live performances please take care
